newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares end at record highs, outlook good.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares end at record highs, outlook good.

text.p: The Bel-20 leading Belgian share index set a second consecutive closing high on Monday, extending the rapid rise into record territory it embarked upon last month and with no end to the bull run in sight.
One dealer said the market should remain well supported ... "as long as the dollar keeps up to these levels and interest rates remain low".

He was confident too of support from further gains on Wall Street, which suffered some profit taking on Monday. "With all these share buy backs we're seeing there, institutions will have more money to invest - it's got to go higher," he added.

The Bel-20 leading share index closed 8.08 points or 0.39 percent firmer at 2,088.58, after setting a fresh intra-day high of 2,090.79 and continuing its rapid rise from below the 1,900 level where it stood early last month.
One share to miss out on Monday's gains was chemicals stock Solvay, which shed 1.6 percent to 12,325 francs.

The weakness follows preliminary 1996 results last week which were lower than some expectations, and a conference call on Friday between analysts and Solvay. Generale Bank noted afterwards that new capacities in peroxides and polypropylene plastics were expected to weigh on sales prices and margins.
Retailer Delhaize, up 1.3 percent at 1,975 francs, and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, 3.2 percent higher at 7,200, both benefited from the dollar's relative strength to the franc.
The U.S. currency actually weakened slightly from Friday's levels, though at 34.17 francs remains well up on the level of 31.78 francs where it stood at the start of 1997.
